results.title: Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs | ServerCalc
results.author: ServerCalc Editorial
highlights:
# Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs

Nebius lifted pay-as-you-go GPU rates up to 21% on October 1 — H100 to $4.50 an hour, B300 to $9.50 — the second rise since spring as AI capacity sells out.

October 12, 2026 ServerCalc Editorial 5 min read

The capacity squeeze that has been pushing up VPS prices all year sits at the other end of the market too, on the GPU servers that AI workloads run on. One of the larger listed GPU clouds, Nebius, has just moved its on-demand prices again — the second time it has done so since the spring — and the new rates are a useful marker for anyone pricing an AI server rather than a plain VPS.

## What changed

From October 1, 2026, Nebius raised its on-demand, pay-as-you-go rates across its four current Nvidia platforms. On its own published price list the per-GPU-hour numbers now read: H100 NVLink at $4.50, up from $3.85 (about 17%); H200 NVLink at $5.40, up from $4.50 (20%); B200 NVLink at $8.50, up from $7.15 (about 19%); and B300 NVLink at $9.50, up from $7.85 (21%). CPU-only servers were caught in the same round — the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU now lists at $0.015 per CPU-hour, roughly a quarter more than before. Separately, from October 8 the provider moved preemptible capacity for these platforms onto dynamic spot pricing, so the cheap interruptible tier no longer has a fixed rate.

These are list prices for on-demand use. Committed and reserved terms are quoted separately and run well below the hourly rate; the increase lands hardest on buyers who pay by the hour with no commitment.

...

The hourly figures are small, but GPU servers run continuously and in multiples, so they add up fast. A single H100 left running around the clock for a 730-hour month now costs about $3,285 on demand, against roughly $2,810 before October 1 — close to $475 a month more for the same card. Nvidia's NVLink parts are usually taken eight to a node, and an 8×H100 box now runs $36 an hour, or about $26,280 a month flat out, up from near $22,480 — a jump of roughly $3,800 a month per node. On the newest silicon the numbers are larger again: a B300 is $9.50 an hour, so an eight-GPU B300 node is $76 an hour, more than $55,000 a month.

...

In early May the same H100 listed at $2.95 an hour; at $4.50 it is about 53% higher in roughly five months, and the B300 has moved from $6.10 to $9.50 over the same stretch.

...

Nebius has not tied the increase to the cost of any one component. Its own executives have described a market where demand outruns supply: the company has said it sold capacity as fast as it could bring it online, and that it could sell its entire 2027 capacity on current deal terms. That is the same story driving the memory and storage shortages we have covered from the VPS side — capacity, power and advanced-packaging supply are the bottleneck, and when a provider cannot build fast enough, the on-demand price is the lever it pulls first. A hardware generation that is nominally faster per dollar does not help if you cannot get time on it at the old rate.

...

Per-GPU-hour rates across the GPU clouds still vary by a factor of two or more for the same card, and the headline price is only part of it — egress, storage and the minimum node size all land in the bill. Our AI workload page sets out how to size the server to the model rather than to the marketing, and the catalog lets you line providers up on price per resource instead of per press release.

Figures in this piece are from Nebius's published compute pricing page and from reporting by The Motley Fool on the October 1 increase, cross-checked against the provider's own effective-date notice.

If your GPU bills have been creeping up this year, it isn't your imagination. The most visible signal came from Nebius, which put through a blanket price increase across its GPU cloud services effective October 1, 2026, averaging roughly 20% across multiple chip models including the H100 and H200 — its second round of increases since May, according to EQS Newswire reporting on the announcement.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

results.title: AI Compute Cost Outlook: Quarterly Briefing · AgentFlare
highlights:
### Pricing is high at the hyperscalers, discounted elsewhere

As of early November, H100 on-demand pricing ranged from roughly $6.88 per GPU-hour at AWS to $11.06 at Google Cloud, versus approximately $3.90–$6.16 across major neoclouds. [5] H200 pricing reached $10.60 per hour on Google Cloud, while B200 capacity was generally available through flexible-start or committed products rather than standard on-demand listings. [4] 

The spread is economically material: hyperscaler list prices averaged nearly twice GPU-cloud medians across H100, H200, and B200 instances. [1] This creates a strong incentive for workload migration, capacity brokering, and multicloud arbitrage—particularly for inference jobs with predictable utilization.

### Effective cost is falling through commitments and utilization

Reservation economics are increasingly decisive. One-year commitments reduce median GPU pricing by about 21%, while three-year commitments cut it by approximately 48% versus on-demand rates. [1] Google’s three-year H100 commitment was listed at $4.86 per GPU-hour, compared with an $11.06 on-demand rate; its H200 equivalent was $4.65 versus $10.60. [4]

...

### Outlook: lower effective prices, firm premium hardware

Expect advertised hyperscaler GPU rates to remain sticky through the next two quarters, with selective increases where supply is tight—AWS raised several U.S. GPU configurations by about 15% in October after earlier 2026 increases. [9] Effective market pricing should nevertheless decline as neocloud supply expands and long-term discounts deepen.

The key distinction is between GPU-hour price and cost per useful token. The latter should fall faster, favoring inference platforms with superior utilization and software efficiency rather than operators owning the largest nominal fleet.

...

results.title: GPU prices explained | Intelaris
results.author: Intelaris Research
highlights:
Published Oct 9, 2026

## Price per GPU-hour

Cloud providers quote GPU capacity per GPU and hour. A server with eight GPUs costs eight times the GPU-hour price per hour.

Storage, outbound data transfer and support are usually charged separately.

## Pricing models

On-demand: billed by the hour, no commitment. Reserved: fixed capacity for one or three years at a lower price per hour.

Spot: unused capacity at a discount that the provider can reclaim. Community and marketplace: capacity from third parties, with varying reliability.

## Location, currency and availability

The same GPU costs different amounts in different regions. Providers quote in different currencies, for example USD, EUR or CHF.

A list price does not guarantee available capacity. AI Compute Prices shows availability where the source reports it.

## Spread in the market

For the H100, on-demand prices range from USD 2.65 EUR 2.38 CHF 2.20 to USD 14.38 EUR 12.92 CHF 11.93 per GPU-hour, with a median of USD 3.89 EUR 3.50 CHF 3.23, as of Nov 11, 2026.

As of Nov 11, 2026, 21:05 UTC Source: public price lists and pricing APIs of the providers Converted at ECB reference rates of Nov 11, 2026 Method

results.title: The Cheapest H100 Is Out of Stock: What 25 Clouds of GPU Pricing Data Shows | beCloudReady
results.author: Chandan Kumar
highlights:
We track hourly GPU prices across 25 clouds every night. The cheapest H100 on our list is out of stock, and most providers do not publish stock at all. Here is what the data shows and how we handle it.

On 14 October 2026 the lowest H100 price in our tracker was $1.66 per GPU-hour, listed by Latitude. That row is marked out of stock. The cheapest H100 that a provider says you can rent right now is $3.30 per GPU-hour, at Scaleway. That is almost double.

...

GPU Price is a free tracker we run for the data and AI teams we train. A scraper runs every night and publishes on-demand, per-GPU-hour prices from public pricing APIs and catalogs.

...

After this week's changes, the 14 October snapshot has:

- 518 priced offers across 25 providers (up from 436 offers and 18 providers before the change)
- Hyperscalers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle) and GPU-specialist clouds in the same table
- A per-GPU-hour price, so an 8-GPU node and a single-GPU instance compare fairly

...

## What the data shows on 14 October

Median per-GPU-hour price of the offers in the tracker (not matched by instance size, so read these as a market snapshot rather than a benchmark):

| GPU | Offers | Providers | Lowest listed | Median | Highest listed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 50 | 17 | $1.66 (Latitude, out of stock) | $3.25 | $10.00 (Oracle) |
| H200 | 21 | 10 | $2.25 (Excess Supply, out of stock) | $5.29 | $10.60 (Azure) |
| B200 | 17 | 9 | $3.74 (BoostRun, out of stock) | $7.79 | $14.24 (AWS) |
| A100 80GB | 45 | 14 | $1.35 (Excess Supply, in stock) | $1.98 | $4.10 (Azure) |
| L40S | 46 | 12 | $0.69 (BoostRun, out of stock) | $1.70 | $7.58 (AWS) |

Three things stand out.

1. The cheapest listing is usually not rentable. For H100, H200, B200 and L40S the lowest listed price is marked out of stock. For H100, 27 of the 50 offers are out of stock, 3 are in stock and 20 are unknown. A ranking that ignores this tells you to go to a provider that has nothing to sell you.

2. Hyperscalers cost about twice as much at the median. The median H100 offer is $5.75 per GPU-hour on the four hyperscalers and $2.73 on everyone else. For A100 80GB it is $3.55 against $1.52. Some of that gap is real capacity guarantees, networking and enterprise terms. Some of it is simply price. Whether the gap is worth paying is a decision about your workload, and a price table cannot make it for you.

...

For H100, 20 of 50 offers have no stock data. The cheapest in-stock H100 we can verify is $3.30, but a direct provider with no stock signal could be cheaper and rentable.
- Marketplace prices can include a markup. Shadeform resells capacity from other clouds. A marketplace price may differ from the same provider's own price page, and the marketplace may list a provider that also appears elsewhere.
- On-demand only. Spot, reserved and committed-use prices are excluded. They can change the ranking.
- Stock changes within hours. The snapshot is nightly. Treat it as where to look first, not as a reservation.
- Per-GPU price is not total cost. Egress, storage, minimum commitments and setup time are not in the number.

...

Data: public provider pricing APIs and catalogs, snapshot of 14 October 2026.
